source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Agent turns a failure signal into a written self-reflection kept in memory (last 3). It beats baselines that just retry.
numbers: AlfWorld (134 tasks): +22 points absolute over 12 trials. HotPotQA (100 q): +20 points. HumanEval Python pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%. ReAct-only never solved a task failed on trial 1; ReAct hallucination rate stuck at 22%.
limits: Authors' own benchmarks; HumanEval 91% depends on self-written unit tests; small samples.
agent_relevance: Strong support for storing a verbal lesson per failure, but the lesson needs a trustworthy failure signal.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Ablation: a written explanation of the failure adds value beyond simply replaying the last failed trajectory.
numbers: HotPotQA CoT(GT), 100 q: self-reflection gives +8 points absolute over episodic-memory-only (most recent trajectory). Reflexion also fixed 14 points of questions that CoT(GT) got wrong (39% unsolved at baseline).
limits: 100 questions; one model family (GPT-3.5 era).
agent_relevance: Keep the explanation of why it failed, not only the failed case itself (the Schank/Kolodner idea).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Two ablations on HumanEval-Rust hardest 50: without test generation, reflection hurts; without the explanation step, no gain.
numbers: Base 0.60. Reflexion 0.68. No test generation (reflect blindly) 0.52. Tests but no natural-language reflection 0.60.
limits: 50 problems, GPT-4, single run; verbose Rust compiler errors help.
agent_relevance: Reflection with no external check can be worse than doing nothing: harmful edits to correct answers. Needs a verifier or a gate.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: Failure case: Reflexion did not improve on WebShop and produced unhelpful reflections.
numbers: 100 WebShop environments, 2-shot ReAct+Reflexion, stopped after 4 trials with no improvement.
limits: Authors say tasks needing diverse, creative exploration are a local-minimum trap for reflection.
agent_relevance: Lessons from failure do not replace exploration. Add exploration or restart when reflections stop changing the action.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: False-positive rate of self-written tests limits the loop.
numbers: MBPP Python false positive test pass 16.3% vs HumanEval Python 1.4%; baseline 80% vs 82%; Reflexion overall 91% on HumanEval.
limits: Gains shrink where the self-check is wrong.
agent_relevance: A wrong 'it passed' signal blocks learning from the failure. Failure detection quality is the bottleneck.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Learns rules (ADD/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE/EDIT list of insights) by comparing success and failure pairs, then retrieves similar successes. Both parts matter.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieve-only: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%, ALFWorld 50% vs 55%, WebShop 37% vs 38% (WebShop reward 0.675 vs 0.67). Full ExpeL ALFWorld 59% vs Reflexion R3 54%; HotpotQA ExpeL 40% at R3 equals Reflexion 39%. 4-fold validation; HotpotQA 100 q, ALFWorld 134 tasks, WebShop 100 tasks.
limits: Small test sets; ReAct and Reflexion prompts reused.
agent_relevance: Combine abstract lessons with concrete retrieved cases; which helps more depends on the task.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Ablations on how insights are made. LLM-learned insights beat hand-written ones, adding raw reflections to insight extraction hurts, and a stronger extractor helps.
numbers: HotpotQA SR: ReAct 28.0, hand-crafted insights 32.0, insights built with reflections 29.0, gpt-3.5 extractor 32.0, full ExpeL (gpt-4) 39.0.
limits: Authors guess reflections sometimes hallucinate and mislead the extractor; not tested.
agent_relevance: Feed a lesson-writer verified success/failure contrasts, not unverified self-stories. Use the strongest model for synthesis.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Experience quality and diversity drive the gain; contrast pairs (a fail and a later success on the same task) are the raw material. Retrieval by task similarity beats reason similarity and random.
numbers: ALFWorld SR: ReAct 40.0, random sampled successes 42.5, reason-similarity retrieval 48.5, task-similarity (ExpeL) 59.0. Extracting insights only from the few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct.
limits: ALFWorld only for the retrieval ablation.
agent_relevance: Retrieve by task similarity; failure lessons need real experience, not invented ones.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: scaling agent self-evolving with reasoning memory
finding: Memory items distilled from both successes and failures (title, description, content; at most 3 per trajectory) beat memory from successes only and memory-free agents.
numbers: WebArena overall success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points over memory-free across three backbones. Up to 20% relative gain and fewer steps (reduction up to 26.9% relative on successful cases).
limits: Google authors; WebArena, Mind2Web, SWE-Bench-Verified; labels come from an LLM judge, not ground truth.
agent_relevance: Direct modern evidence that failure lessons add value beyond success-only memory.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: scaling agent self-evolving with reasoning memory
finding: Failures help only if the memory design can digest them. Baselines built for successes get worse or flat when failures are added.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash, no memory 39.0. Synapse 40.6 -> 41.7 with failures. AWM 44.4 -> 42.2 with failures. ReasoningBank 46.5 (success only) -> 49.7 (with failures).
limits: Single subset and backbone for this ablation.
agent_relevance: Naive dumping of failed cases can hurt. Distil each failure into a lesson with a cause.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: scaling agent self-evolving with reasoning memory
finding: Robust to a noisy success/failure judge; AWM did not transfer across websites while ReasoningBank did.
numbers: Simulated judge accuracy swept from 100% down to 50%; similar success rates across 70-90%; best at 100%. On the WebArena Multi subset ReasoningBank gained +4.6 over the strongest baseline while AWM degraded.
limits: Noise was simulated by flipping labels, not real judge bias; paper admits judge errors on ambiguous tasks.
agent_relevance: A rough failure label is enough if lessons are distilled; 50% (random) is the floor.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Success-only workflow memory: strong gains, so it is the comparison point against failure-aware memory.
numbers: WebArena: +12.0 points absolute over BrowserGym baseline, 51.1% relative (23.5 -> 35.5 overall); 7.6% relative above SteP, which uses human workflows. Mind2Web relative +24.6% (abstract). About 2.0 fewer steps per task.
limits: Memory built only from successes; online version relies on self-judged trajectories.
agent_relevance: A success-only library is already good. Failure lessons must beat it, as ReasoningBank claims.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Wrong self-judged workflows can degrade performance; offline and online memories combined did not add up.
numbers: Mind2Web cross-domain SR (gpt-4): AWM offline 36.4 vs online 40.9; combined 39.3, between the two. Paper: online workflows from predicted trajectories are not always correct and can degrade.
limits: Mind2Web success rates are small in absolute terms.
agent_relevance: Memory quality control matters more than quantity; a bad lesson can persist.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following behavior
finding: Found an experience-following property: when the new task looks like a stored one, the agent copies the stored output. So wrong stored records spread (error propagation).
numbers: Four agents (incl. EHRAgent, AgentDriver, RegAgent, CIC-IoT). Add-all and weak-evaluator additions gave flat or declining success over time; fixed memory often beat them; strict (ground-truth) selective addition kept improving, and in AgentDriver passed the error-free-memory variant after about 2000 executions.
limits: Strict evaluator uses ground truth or human; a judge fine-tuned on 300 trajectories gave strong but lower gains.
agent_relevance: Do not store a failed or wrong run as a model to copy. A lesson must be marked as what not to do and gated by a reliable check.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following behavior
finding: History-based deletion removes records whose later use gave poor results; also misaligned replay: correct-looking old records can mislead.
numbers: Combined periodic and history-based deletion with a strict evaluator gave the best performance/size balance; a capacity-limited memory (100 records EHRAgent, 180 AgentDriver) still did well against the fixed baseline.
limits: Depends on evaluator reliability; with weak evaluators deletion results vary.
agent_relevance: Track whether each lesson helped when retrieved; prune lessons that did not (case-base maintenance).

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
finding: Much of the self-correction gain in earlier work (including Reflexion's) came from oracle labels that tell the model when to stop. Without them, accuracy fell.
numbers: With oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9->84.3, CSQA 75.8->89.7, HotpotQA 26.0->29.0; GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0->59.0. Intrinsic (no oracle), after 2 rounds: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 74.7, CSQA 41.8 (from 75.8); GPT-4 GSM8K 89.0 (from 95.5), HotpotQA 43.0 (from 49.0).
limits: Reasoning tasks only; Reflexion's HotpotQA sample (100 q) is small; later and trained models behave differently.
agent_relevance: Failure lessons are worthless if the agent cannot tell it failed. Get an external failure signal.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When can LLMs actually correct their own mistakes? A critical survey of self-correction
finding: Survey of self-correction studies. Conclusions: no prior work shows successful self-correction from prompted-LLM feedback in general tasks; it works where reliable external feedback exists; large-scale fine-tuning enables it; some tasks suit it by nature.
numbers: Qualitative survey; the bottleneck named is feedback generation (error finding), not fixing.
quote: no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs in general tasks
limits: Survey to 2024; some claims depend on how research questions are framed.
agent_relevance: Design the schema so the failure signal comes from a check (tests, tools, ground truth), not self-opinion.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Finding the first mistake is the hard part. Fixing it, once located, works.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake: 2186 PaLM 2 traces, 5 tasks. Best model GPT-4 only 52.87% overall at locating the first error. Backtracking with oracle location on word sorting: 23.53% of wrong-answer traces fixed vs 11.11% of right-answer traces broken. Backtracking losses plateau near 65% mistake-finding accuracy; gains exceed losses at roughly 60-70%.
limits: Traces from one model (PaLM 2 Unicorn); logic mistakes only; a small classifier trained out of domain helped 4 of 5 tasks but did not reach the 65% bar.
agent_relevance: Credit assignment (which step failed) is the weak link in a lesson. Store the step, not just that it failed.

source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench: the self-correction blind spot
finding: Models fix an error placed in the user turn but not the same error in their own turn: a blind spot. Likely a training-data effect.
numbers: 14 open non-reasoning models: 64.5% average blind spot. External errors triggered 179.5% more correction markers on GSM8K-SC. Appending 'Wait' cut the blind spot by 89.3%; LoRA on 5,306 error-correction traces cut it by 76.0%.
limits: Mostly synthetic injected errors; mechanistic steering shown only in two 7-8B models; reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot.
agent_relevance: Present stored failures as external critiques ('a previous attempt did X') and add a prompt to pause and re-check.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Learning from failure: negative-aware training for LLM agents
finding: Fine-tuning on failed trajectories helps only when they are tagged as failures (prefix/suffix). Mixing them in untagged can hurt.
numbers: Math, LLaMA-2-7B with 2k positive examples: +8.74 points over positives-only; 13B with 5k positives: only +0.52. HotpotQA NAT-2: +2 EM, +6 F1 over no negatives. Gain saturates near 11k negatives, shrinks as positives grow; low-quality negatives worsen results.
limits: Earlier work (Zeng et al. 2023) found negatives harmed; this paper says quantity and quality explain the conflict. Trajectories from GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Same lesson for prompts: label failures clearly as failures; value is largest when good examples are scarce.

source: Bensal et al. (2025) Reflect, Retry, Reward: self-improving LLMs via RL
finding: Training a model only to write better reflections after a failed first try (reward if the retry succeeds) gave large gains with binary feedback.
numbers: Up to +34.7% on Countdown equation writing and +18.1% on APIGen function calling. Average +4.5% from a prompted second attempt with reflection on APIGen. Fine-tuned 1.5B-7B models beat same-family models 10 times larger.
limits: Needs a verifiable binary signal; training, so not directly our scaffold-only setting; the paper's related work says reflection works best when base accuracy is low and verification exists.
agent_relevance: Reflection quality is learnable but also promptable; restrict reflection to verified failures.

source: An et al. (2024) Learning from mistakes makes LLM better reasoner (LEMA)
finding: Fine-tuning with (mistake step, why it is wrong, corrected solution) triples written by GPT-4 beats fine-tuning on correct solutions alone.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B: GSM8K 83.5 vs 81.4; MATH 25.0 vs 23.6, 29.3 with correction-centric evolution; CSQA 84.2 -> 85.3. At equal token budget, mixing CoT and correction data beat either alone. Gains of 0.3 to 4.6 points on other models.
limits: Small gains (1 to 3 points typical); corrector is GPT-4; moderately hard questions work best as seeds.
agent_relevance: Explained mistakes (step, reason, fix) are the right lesson format, mirroring Schank's explained failures.

source: Zhu et al. (2025) Where LLM agents fail and how they can learn from failures (AgentDebug)
finding: A taxonomy of agent failures (memory, reflection, planning, action, system) from 500+ failed trajectories; main finding is that early errors cascade. Root-cause feedback beats broad feedback.
numbers: AgentErrorBench: 200 annotated trajectories (100 ALFWorld, 50 WebShop, 50 GAIA). Error location all-correct accuracy 24.3% vs 0.3% best baseline; step accuracy 45.0% vs 28.0%. ALFWorld success after feedback: GPT-4o-mini 21 -> 55, Qwen3-8B 48 -> 74, Qwen3-Next-80B 60 -> 84; up to 26% relative gain across benchmarks.
limits: All-correct localisation still only 24.3%, so most root causes are missed; annotation by 10 graduate students.
agent_relevance: Index lessons by root-cause failure type and by the earliest wrong step.

source: Hammond (1986, 1990) CHEF: case-based planning, explaining and repairing plans that fail
finding: Classic failure-driven CBR. CHEF stores a failed plan, explains it causally, links the predictive features to the failure, picks a repair strategy by failure type, and warns on future similar goals. (Opened a secondary summary page, not the original paper.)
numbers: Example: beef-and-broccoli, broccoli soggy from liquid; repair SPLIT-AND-REFORM; later warned on chicken and snow peas. 20 TOPs known; domain Szechwan cooking. No quantitative test in the summary.
limits: No benchmark numbers; multi-cause failures have no single item to blame; some repairs too complex to reuse; hand-built causal rules; one domain.
agent_relevance: Origin of lessons with traps: index the failure by predictive features, generalize one level (beef to meat). Needs a causal explanation, which an LLM must supply and may get wrong.

source: Hammond (1987) Explaining and repairing plans that fail (IJCAI-87, pp 109-114)
finding: Abstract confirms causal explanations of failure retrieve abstract repair strategies that become specific plan edits, and can also fix plans found faulty before running.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Only abstract read; the original has no controlled evaluation.
agent_relevance: Run the stored trap check before acting (pre-execution repair), not only after failure.
